newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian banks bet on explosion in credit - report.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian banks bet on explosion in credit - report.

text.p: The Central Bank's loosening of credit restrictions has prompted Brazilian banks to expand loans for industry, trade and individuals, a local financial newspaper said.
A survey by Gazeta Mercantil newspaper said the country's leading financial institutions expect credit transactions to rise by a moderate 15 to 25 percent in the second half.
"Consumers themselves have rejected excessive indebtedness," Bradesco Vice President Antonio Bornia was quoted by the paper as saying.
The newspaper said banks are emphasizing personal loans, a sector which presents reduced risk and the greatest potential for growth.

Caution in extending credit can be explained by the high rate of unpaid loans, which rose from 11.5 percent of total loans to 21.5 percent between May 1995 and the same month this year, the paper said.
A study by the Central Bank showed that late repayment and written off credits to the private sector grew from 19.4 billion reais to 38.2 billion reais in that period, it added.
